_doc: The single-source-of-truth registry: each CAPABILITY has exactly ONE home; all callers use it. Read by the honestreview `canonical_concerns` doctrine (write-time) and tests/test_canonical_concerns.py (suite). Adding a concern is a deliberate act: give it a home, a one-line description, and a `telltale` (what its operations look like, so a reviewer can locate candidate sites). `status`: 'enforced' = one home today, the gate checks it; 'consolidating' = home chosen, callers still being moved. See docs/SINGLE_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md.

concerns.description: THE one authoring home for per-model data — one typed record per model: id, aliases, retired_alias_of, provider, metered_id, lane_spellings (lane->use-name), price (in/out/cached/batch, with source+verified provenance), output_ceiling, context_window, reasoning (style/floor/default/levels/reasons_by_default), roles. Every model FACT is authored here ONCE. Derived copies are fine ONLY if generated+fresh+never hand-edited: prices.json is GENERATED from this (carries a _generated marker); the synced LiteLLM cache is a BREADTH fallback for models not in the catalog. PUBLISHED fields (price/ceiling) carry the PROVIDER as origin (provenance + a verified date); INTERNAL decisions (lane<->metered spelling, chosen reasoning floor) are authored here. A price literal, a ceiling table, a reasoning-floor, or an alias mapping authored ANYWHERE ELSE is the defect this concern blocks.
concerns.telltale: authoring or deciding ANY model fact — a price/rate literal, an output-ceiling value, a reasoning floor/default, a lane<->metered id spelling, an alias/retired-alias mapping, or a default/probe/panel model id — for a specific model

concerns.description: The RESOLVER for a model's maximum OUTPUT tokens (published catalog value > live /models > learned-fact-floored > backstop); NEVER below OUTPUT_FLOOR unless a genuinely-published max is lower. The published ceiling VALUE is owned by model_catalog (not held here); this resolver reads it. The ceiling is not the cost.
concerns.telltale: resolving or clamping a per-model output-token ceiling / max_output for a call or estimate

concerns.description: The OUTPUT max_tokens actually SENT for a call = the model CEILING (output_ceiling: real published max, or the 32K floor). The CALLER'S requested max_tokens is IGNORED (spendguard owns it); max_output is billed on ACTUAL tokens, so the max is free and only too-little truncates. All five send paths route through this — _call_guarded, vendor_call.call, submit.build_chat_batch_jsonl, zai_exec._output_budget, and crossllm (delegates) — none decides the budget itself. Sizing EXPECTED output for a cost estimate is a DIFFERENT concern (expected_output.expect).
concerns.telltale: deciding the max_tokens value to send on a model call (floor/ceiling/caller-value/recommend math)

concerns.description: Whether the INPUT fits the model's input window — REFUSES an over-window input, never truncates it. Input is never silently clipped anywhere.
concerns.telltale: checking or bounding input/prompt size against a model input window; any slice of prompt/content fed to a model

concerns.description: Mapping a requested reasoning tier (minimal|low|medium|high) to the reasoning_effort value a given model actually accepts (only the floor varies per model).
concerns.telltale: translating a reasoning tier to a wire reasoning_effort per model

concerns.description: The cost MATH and price-resolution engine ($/token -> realtime/batch dollars; provider disambiguation; layering). The per-token RATES themselves are owned by model_catalog (curated) — prices.json is a GENERATED projection of the catalog, and the synced LiteLLM cache is the breadth fallback; pricing.py resolves and computes, it does not author rates.
concerns.telltale: computing dollars from token counts, or the price-resolution/layering logic (NOT authoring a per-model rate — that is model_catalog)

concerns.description: The canonical predicate for 'this exception IS a deliberate spend/budget refusal or deadline that must propagate, never be swallowed by a fail-open handler.'
concerns.telltale: deciding whether an exception is a deliberate stop / refusal to re-raise

concerns.description: The ONE $0 snapshot of the admission + queue + reasoning-economics picture that the CLI (`spendguard dispatch`) and the MCP tool render identically.
